models.name: Airway-Scale Deposition CFD Model
models.what_it_computes: Transient airflow from oral cavity to segmental bronchi with polydisperse particle tracking to estimate regional and lobar deposition fractions, wall impaction hotspots, residence time distributions, and delivered lung dose.

models.name: Device–Mouth–Throat Jet CFD Model
models.what_it_computes: Device-resolved propellant jet, spacer flow, and mouth–throat transport using transient turbulence and evaporating droplets to compute entry-plane particle size–velocity–angle distributions and oropharyngeal deposition.

mechanisms.name: Jet-Driven Inertial Impaction During Actuation–Inhalation Overlap
mechanisms.why_it_matters: High-velocity plumes increase oropharyngeal losses and reduce delivered lung dose; controlling impaction determines efficiency and local side-effect risk.

mechanisms.name: Sedimentation and Diffusion During Post-Inhalation Breath-Hold
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Low-flow transport and pause enhance distal deposition of fine particles, affecting therapeutic reach to small airways.

spans: Airflow boundary conditions for the airway model followed the coached adult profile described earlier.

The inlet pressure at the mouth was set such that the target volumetric flow rates were achieved; the tracheal outlet split into lobar outlets with resistive elements tuned to match expected lobe flow distributions at steady 0.5 L/s inhalation based on morphometric ratios (right upper 16%, right middle 8%, right lower 26%, left upper 22%, left lower 28%).

findings.mechanism: Sedimentation and Diffusion During Post-Inhalation Breath-Hold
spans: Within the breath-hold mechanism, the airway model’s lobar fractions and residence times are sensitive primarily to particle size and the duration of the hold.
Reducing the hold to 0 s (i.e., no pause) yielded a delivered lung dose of 32.7% (1.2 points relative to 5 s), with a smaller distal share and a median distal residence time of 1.7 s.
Extending the hold to 10 s increased delivered lung dose to 34.8% (+0.9 points relative to 5 s), and lengthened the median dwell time by 0.7 s.
findings.span: Within the breath-hold mechanism, the airway model’s lobar fractions and residence times are sensitive primarily to particle size and the duration of the hold.

findings.mechanism: Sedimentation and Diffusion During Post-Inhalation Breath-Hold
spans: For the breath-hold mechanism, where velocities are low and the flow is laminarizing, turbulence closure choice had negligible effect on distal deposition, which was dominated by particle size and gravity with Brownian motion adding dispersion for the smallest sizes.

findings.mechanism: Jet-Driven Inertial Impaction During Actuation–Inhalation Overlap
findings.factor: Relevance of the quantities of interest
spans: The first mechanism is jet-driven inertial impaction during the overlap of device actuation and inhalation.

The outputs that inform this mechanism are oropharyngeal deposition fraction, laryngeal hot-spot identification, peak and time-integrated wall shear near the laryngeal inlet, and the detailed SVA distribution at the entry plane into the lower airways.
The device–mouth–throat model delivered a nominal oropharyngeal deposition fraction of 19.4% of the emitted dose under coached timing and flow.
findings.span: The first mechanism is jet-driven inertial impaction during the overlap of device actuation and inhalation.

findings.mechanism: Jet-Driven Inertial Impaction During Actuation–Inhalation Overlap
spans: Source code resided in a distributed version control system with branch protection and code review requirements; each release was tagged and accompanied by a change log.

Unit test coverage across the numerical kernels was 97% by line count, and 64 regression tests—including multiphase nozzle discharge, evaporating sprays in quiescent chambers, and particle settling in a laminar duct—ran nightly.

Configuration management ensured that all input decks, meshes, and scripts for the cases reported here were archived with unique identifiers and hashes; a reader or auditor could reproduce a case by pulling a single manifest path.
findings.span: Source code resided in a distributed version control system with branch protection and code review requirements; each release was tagged and accompanied by a change log.

findings.mechanism: Jet-Driven Inertial Impaction During Actuation–Inhalation Overlap
spans: Device actuation parameters were taken from a dedicated nozzle test rig.

The mass of propellant discharged per actuation (12.5 mg) was determined by pre/post weighing with a precision of 0.1 mg over 30 shots; the time-resolved discharge profile was inferred from high-speed schlieren imaging and a calibrated piezoelectric transducer at the nozzle, producing a peak discharge at 35 ms and a trailing tail to 120 ms.

Inspiratory valve pressure–flow characteristics for the VHC were measured in a bench rig with step flows from 0.1 to 1.0 L/s; the modeled porous membrane resistance curve reproduced a measured pressure drop of 105 Pa at 0.5 L/s within 3 Pa.
findings.span: Device actuation parameters were taken from a dedicated nozzle test rig.

findings.mechanism: Jet-Driven Inertial Impaction During Actuation–Inhalation Overlap
spans: Two deviations from coached technique are explicitly explored to assess robustness to user missteps: (i) early actuation at t = 0.1 s (100 ms before inhalation begins) and t = 0.3 s (300 ms early), and (ii) late actuation at t = 0.5 s (300 ms late).

The early actuation case at 0.3 s moved the bulk of the jet toward the chamber walls before uptake, leading to larger droplets reaching the MT upon inhalation and increasing oropharyngeal deposition from 19.4% to 27.8% (+8.4 points).
findings.span: Two deviations from coached technique are explicitly explored to assess robustness to user missteps: (i) early actuation at t = 0.1 s (100 ms before inhalation begins) and t = 0.3 s (300 ms early), and (ii) late actuation at t = 0.5 s (300 ms late).
